title: docs(readme): a 30-second demo GIF opens the README, rendered from a real showcase run
body:
Fixes #22232
Clause-②: no

Part A of the card: the README now opens on a thirty-second GIF recorded from a really running app, rendered by a committed script. Part B (repository topics and the About line) is the maintainer's click on the repository settings page and is not in this PR.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|:---|:---|
| `docs/screenshots/readme-demo.gif` | new: 1200 x 675, 43 frames, 29.88 s, loops forever, **497,614 bytes** |
| `docs/screenshots/render-readme-demo.mjs` | new: the generator (boots the app, makes the calls, screenshots the Console, renders the frames, assembles the GIF) |
| `README.md` | top only: the GIF replaces the embedded cover image under the chip row, a one-line caption names the three beats, the "Watch: ObjectStack in 90 Seconds" link stays as text under it. `docs/screenshots/hero-cover-dark.png` is byte-untouched (the docs site's og:image). The architecture diagram and everything below it are unchanged. |

No `packages/**`, `apps/docs`, `content/**`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `package.json` change; nothing publishes.

## The recording

Example and object: `examples/app-showcase`, object `showcase_team` (three fields, so the whole typed definition fits one frame without scrolling).

1. **One definition, and the app runs.** The Team object exactly as `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/team.object.ts` declares it (comment lines omitted; the frame says so), then `pnpm dev:showcase -- --fresh -p PORT` booting it on a throwaway database, then the Console's Team list (2 rows).
2. **An agent creates a record over MCP.** A JSON-RPC `tools/call` of `create_record` against the running app's `/api/v1/mcp`, sent with the dev admin's API key; the real response; then the Console list with the new "Data Guild" row (3 rows) and its record page reading "Created by Dev Admin".
3. **A read-only identity is refused.** The byte-identical call sent with the Auditor persona's API key; the real refusal; then the Console list, unchanged (3 rows).

Closing frame: "The ontology is the software." and the four chips Executable · AI-writable · Agent-operable · You own it.

Measured in the run that rendered the committed GIF (port 39497): `showcase_team` went 2 → 3 on the admin's call and stayed 3 on the refused call (read back over REST after each call).

- Admin's call: `200`, record `QZu-Fcgx29Po-Sfn` "Data Guild", `created_by` = the admin's user id.
- Read-only call, the real response bytes:

```json
{"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"You do not have permission to perform this action. Contact your administrator if you need access."}],"isError":true},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}
```

### Keys and identities

- Both keys are minted through the documented `POST /api/v1/keys` (content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, "Headless: API keys"), each from a session opened with `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`.
- Writer: the dev admin that `--fresh` seeds (`admin@objectos.ai`).
- Read-only identity: the showcase's own Auditor persona, `auditor.demo@example.com` ("Ada Auditor (demo)"), which `examples/app-showcase/src/security/seed-approval-demo.ts` provisions on every dev boot. It holds only the `auditor` position, bound to `showcase_auditor` (no Team grant), plus the member baseline `showcase_member_default`, which grants `showcase_team` read and no create. No code was changed to get a refusal. Before the GIF calls it "read-only", the script proves it can read: its `query_records` on `showcase_team` returned both rows.

### Honesty rules, enforced by the script rather than trusted

- Every browser frame is a screenshot of the real Console against the app that run booted; the only additions are an outline around the new row and around the record count.
- The request panel shows the bytes sent: the body is sent pretty-printed, exactly as drawn; the API key is masked after its public prefix.
- The response panel shows the bytes received, with one re-layout for legibility: the escapes inside `result.content[0].text` are drawn as the characters they encode.
- Terminal lines are lines that run's dev server printed, picked by pattern in order, with a dim ellipsis at each gap. A pattern that stops matching is a refusal (exit 5), not a stand-in line.
- No assistant chat transcript, no model identifier, no record the run did not create; the caller is "an agent" / "any MCP client".
- The script also refuses (exit 5) when the admin's call does not create the row, when the read-only identity cannot read the object, when its create is NOT refused, or when the row count moves on the refusal; and (exit 6) when the GIF is not 1200 px wide, runs outside 20-35 s, or exceeds 4,000,000 bytes.

## Re-render

```bash
node docs/screenshots/render-readme-demo.mjs                 # rewrite the committed GIF
node docs/screenshots/render-readme-demo.mjs --out /tmp/demo  # preview: GIF, every frame and story.json, nothing committed touched
```

Prerequisites are the ones `pnpm dev` checks itself: a built workspace (`pnpm build`) and a built Console (`pnpm objectui:build`), plus `ffmpeg` on PATH. Playwright's Chromium is resolved from `examples/app-showcase` (preinstalled binary under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, never `playwright install`), `sharp` from the docs app's Next dependency (it verifies screenshot and GIF dimensions and duration), and ffmpeg assembles the GIF in two passes (palettegen, then paletteuse with bayer dithering). Four end-to-end runs in this container produced the same beats; byte-identity is not a goal (ids, timestamps, port).

**Fonts:** the frames the script draws use Inter and IBM Plex Mono from Google Fonts, the hero cover's pair; all eight faces loaded in the committed render. Without them the script refuses to write the committed GIF (exit 3), as `render-hero-cover.mjs` does; `--out` previews the system fallback (Liberation Sans / DejaVu Sans Mono). The Console screenshots carry the Console's own fonts. No font file is committed.

## Verification

Run on the final head `8336490e` (change set: the three files above, 662 changed lines, the binary counted 0).

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 13 families. All 13 exited 0: check-ci-filter-parity, check-closing-keyword-parity (and its `--self-test`), check-comment-mask-corpus, `@objectstack/lint` check:doc-formula-expressions, check:cross-package-test-inputs, check:doc-anchors, check:doc-authoring, check:driver-memory-census, check:gitlink-declared, check:nul-bytes, check:refd-timer-probe, check:watch-hint-literal. `--ran` reconciliation: "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
- `pnpm check:published-readme-links` exited 0: "221 outbound link(s) across 101 published markdown file(s) ... 144/144 relative target(s) found in the tree."
- Narrowed eslint, spelled as `pnpm lint` runs it (`--no-inline-config`), over the three changed paths:
  - population, read from the config: `eslint --print-config` answers a config object for `render-readme-demo.mjs` and `undefined` for `README.md` and the GIF;
  - count, read from `--format json`: 3 results, 1 file linted with 0 errors and 0 warnings, 2 "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied";
  - invariance: that config's `parserOptions` is `{ ecmaVersion, sourceType }` with no `project` or `projectService` (type-aware linting is off repo-wide), and nothing imports the new script, so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- Not run locally: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the rest of CI's farm, which CI owns.

## Acceptance notes

- Serial constraint: #22224 (the README contributor-path section, lower in the file) is still open; `origin/main` at `3ae59661` has no README change since this branch's base `7b926f76`, so no merge was needed. Both PRs edit different hunks of README.md.
- Observed in a fresh `pnpm dev:showcase -- --fresh` boot whose full output was read during this work, not investigated, not filed (outside this card): the boot-diagnostics block prints a `sys_migration` "UNIQUE constraint failed" insert warning, a pre-bind settings read warning, an analytics `admitObjectRead` warning and a sharing-rule "expands to NO recipients" warning. The terminal frame shows none of them because it shows a pattern-picked subset of lines; nothing in the GIF depends on them.
- The MCP refusal is an `isError: true` tool result carrying prose only, with HTTP 200 and no machine-readable error code; the GIF shows it as received.
